clauses.text: This policy is a contract between Autos Poblado and the policyholder named on the declarations page. Once the premium is paid, we provide the protection described in each part of this policy, in the territory set out in Part F.
Coverage runs for the policy period shown on the declarations page. Keeping it in force depends on the policyholder meeting the duties this contract assigns, especially those in Part E.
"You" means the policyholder listed on the declarations page. It also includes that person's spouse or partner while the two share a home.
"We" means Autos Poblado, the company that issues this policy and stands behind it.
"Bodily injury" means any harm to a person's health caused by an accident, including wounds, illness that follows from them and, when it happens, death.
"Property damage" means breaking, destroying or making unusable a physical object that belongs to someone else, such as another car, a fence or a storefront.

"Covered auto" means the vehicle listed on the declarations page and any trailer listed there. A vehicle you buy during the policy period is also a covered auto if you tell us about it within 20 days of taking delivery.
"Trailer" means an unpowered vehicle built to be towed by a private passenger car, such as a small cargo trailer or a compact camper.
"Family member" means someone who lives in your home and is related to you by birth, marriage, civil union or adoption, including children in your legal care.
"Occupying" means being inside a vehicle, climbing in or out of it, or standing next to it while loading it or pushing it by hand.

When an accident involving a covered auto makes an insured legally responsible to someone else for bodily injury or property damage, Autos Poblado pays those damages up to the Part A limit. We also handle the insured's defense against those claims with lawyers we choose, and we may settle a claim whenever we think it wise. Our defense duty stops once our Part A payments reach the limit.

Besides the Part A limit, we cover the insured's reasonable out-of-pocket costs when we ask for help with a claim, including travel to court and up to $150 for each day of work missed, plus the cost of any court bond needed in a case we defend.
Part A does not cover harm that an insured causes on purpose, or harm someone else causes following the insured's instructions.
Part A does not cover damage to things the insured owns or is carrying in the vehicle.
Part A does not cover damage to things the insured has rented, borrowed or is looking after for someone else.
Part A does not cover injuries to the insured's own employees that happen while they are working; those are handled by the applicable workplace injury system.
Part A does not cover accidents that happen while a vehicle is carrying people or goods for pay, including trips booked through a ride app. Friends splitting the cost of a trip is not considered pay.
Part A does not cover an insured who is using a vehicle as part of a business that sells, repairs, washes, parks or stores vehicles.
Part A does not cover anyone driving a vehicle without the owner's permission or without a sound reason to believe they had it.
Part A does not cover accidents during races, speed contests or performance tests, or while practicing for them.
Part A does not pay fines, penalties or damages that a court imposes to punish rather than to repair harm.
Part A does not cover driving a motorcycle, a motorized three-wheeler or any other two- or three-wheeled vehicle.
Part A does not cover using a vehicle you own that is not listed on the declarations page, except a newly bought vehicle that the covered auto definition includes.
Part A does not cover using a vehicle that a family member owns, or that a family member has on hand for regular use, unless that vehicle is listed on the declarations page.

The per-person limit on the declarations page is the most we pay for all bodily injury to one person in one accident. The per-accident limit is the most for all bodily injury in that accident, and the property damage limit is the most for all property damaged. Adding insureds, vehicles or claims does not raise these limits.

If an accident happens outside Corvane and the local law there requires higher minimum limits than this policy has, we apply those higher minimums to that accident. We never pay twice for the same loss.
When a Corvane authority asks for proof that a driver carries liability insurance, this policy serves as that proof, with at least the minimum limits set in the jurisdiction document.

If another liability policy also responds to the accident, we split the payment in proportion to each policy's limits. For a vehicle you do not own, that vehicle's own insurance pays first and we pay what remains.

Autos Poblado pays reasonable medical and funeral costs that result from a traffic accident and are incurred within two years of it. We cover you and your family members whether they are riding in a vehicle or struck by one, and anyone else while occupying your covered auto.
Part B does not pay for injuries suffered on a motorcycle or any other two- or three-wheeled vehicle.
Part B does not pay for injuries suffered while the vehicle is carrying passengers for pay.
Part B does not pay for injuries that happen while the vehicle is being used as a home or as a fixed workplace.
Part B does not pay for injuries suffered in races, speed contests or performance tests.
The per-person limit on the declarations page is the most we pay toward each injured person's medical costs from one accident, however many people or vehicles are involved.
If another medical payments policy covers the same costs, we pay only what is left unpaid after that policy, up to our limit.

Autos Poblado pays the damages for bodily injury that you or a family member are entitled to claim from the driver or owner of an uninsured vehicle. This includes an accident where the vehicle at fault drives off and neither its driver nor its owner can be identified, as long as the police received a report of it.
Part C does not cover injuries to anyone riding in a vehicle owned by you or a family member that is not insured under this policy.
Part C does not cover a claim the insured settled with the at-fault party or its insurer without our written agreement.
Part C does not apply while the vehicle is carrying people or goods for pay.
Part C does not cover anyone using a vehicle without the owner's permission or without a sound reason to believe they had it.

The most we pay under this part is the uninsured motorist limit shown on the declarations page, per person and per accident, however many vehicles or people are involved. Anything the at-fault party has already paid is subtracted.
If several policies cover the same person for the same accident, we split the payment in proportion to each policy's limits.

If we and the insured disagree about whether damages are owed or about how much, either side may ask for the question to be decided by a single arbitrator in Corvane. Each side pays its own costs and half of the arbitrator's fee.

clauses.part: Part D — Coverage for Damage to Your Auto
clauses.text: Autos Poblado pays for sudden, accidental damage to your covered auto from hitting another vehicle or object or from rolling over, minus the collision deductible on the declarations page. We pay even if you caused the crash.

clauses.part: Part D — Coverage for Damage to Your Auto
clauses.text: We also pay, minus the matching deductible, for damage to your covered auto that does not come from a crash: theft of the car or its parts, fire, flood, hail, falling objects, vandalism, broken glass and hitting an animal.

clauses.part: Part D — Coverage for Damage to Your Auto
clauses.text: If your covered auto is out of use because it was stolen or damaged in a covered loss, we reimburse what you spend getting around in the meantime, up to $25 a day and $750 in total. Reimbursement starts on the third day after the theft or damage.

clauses.part: Part D — Coverage for Damage to Your Auto
clauses.text: Part D does not cover damage that happens while the vehicle is carrying people or goods for pay.

clauses.part: Part D — Coverage for Damage to Your Auto
clauses.text: Part D does not cover wear from use, rust, mechanical or electrical failure, or freezing, unless it results from a theft or another covered loss.

clauses.part: Part D — Coverage for Damage to Your Auto
clauses.text: Part D does not cover sound systems, screens, navigation units or other electronics that were not installed at the factory.

clauses.part: Part D — Coverage for Damage to Your Auto
clauses.text: Part D does not cover personal belongings inside the vehicle, such as clothing, tools, cash or phones.

clauses.part: Part D — Coverage for Damage to Your Auto
clauses.text: Part D does not cover damage limited to the tires, such as flats or blowouts, unless it comes from fire, theft or vandalism.

clauses.part: Part D — Coverage for Damage to Your Auto
clauses.text: Part D does not cover losing the vehicle to seizure, impoundment or destruction ordered by an authority.

clauses.part: Part D — Coverage for Damage to Your Auto
clauses.text: Part D does not cover damage caused by war, rebellion, organized terrorism or nuclear energy.

clauses.part: Part D — Coverage for Damage to Your Auto
clauses.text: Part D does not cover damage suffered in races, speed contests or performance tests, or while practicing for them.

clauses.part: Part D — Coverage for Damage to Your Auto
clauses.text: Part D does not cover parts, accessories or modifications added to the vehicle without telling us, such as custom wheels, altered suspension or engine upgrades.

clauses.part: Part D — Coverage for Damage to Your Auto
clauses.text: Part D does not cover damage that you or a family member cause to the vehicle on purpose.

clauses.part: Part D — Coverage for Damage to Your Auto
clauses.text: Part D does not cover damage caused by loading the vehicle beyond the weight its manufacturer allows.

clauses.part: Part D — Coverage for Damage to Your Auto
clauses.text: Part D does not cover theft when the vehicle was left unlocked with the keys inside or with the engine running in a public place.

clauses.part: Part D — Coverage for Damage to Your Auto
clauses.text: Part D does not cover flood damage when the driver entered a road that authorities had closed or marked as flooded.

clauses.part: Part D — Coverage for Damage to Your Auto
clauses.text: The most we pay for a loss is the lower of the vehicle's market value at the time of the loss and the cost of repairing it, or of replacing stolen parts with equivalent ones.

clauses.part: Part D — Coverage for Damage to Your Auto
clauses.text: We choose whether to pay the loss in cash or to arrange the repair or replacement ourselves. If we pay for a total loss, the vehicle or what remains of it becomes ours. If we recover a stolen vehicle, we give it back to you and pay for any damage it suffered.

clauses.part: Part D — Coverage for Damage to Your Auto
clauses.text: This coverage does not benefit anyone who has the vehicle in their care as a business, such as a repair shop, a parking garage or a car transport company; if they caused the damage, we may recover it from them.

clauses.part: Part D — Coverage for Damage to Your Auto
clauses.text: If another policy or source covers the same loss, we pay only our share, in proportion to our limit against the total.

clauses.part: Part D — Coverage for Damage to Your Auto
clauses.text: If we and you disagree on the amount of a loss, each side names an appraiser and the two appraisers choose a third. What any two of the three agree on binds both sides. Each side pays its own appraiser and half of the third.

clauses.part: Part E — Duties After an Accident or Loss
clauses.text: Tell us about any accident or loss as soon as you can, and always within the deadline set in the Corvane jurisdiction document.

clauses.part: Part E — Duties After an Accident or Loss
clauses.text: Tell us how, when and where it happened, and which vehicles and people were involved.

clauses.part: Part E — Duties After an Accident or Loss
clauses.text: Give us the name and a way to reach any injured person and any witness you know of.

clauses.part: Part E — Duties After an Accident or Loss
clauses.text: Work with us as we look into the claim and as we defend any claim made against you.

clauses.part: Part E — Duties After an Accident or Loss
clauses.text: Send us right away a copy of any notice, summons or lawsuit you receive about the accident.

clauses.part: Part E — Duties After an Accident or Loss
clauses.text: If the claim involves injuries, attend the medical exams we request, with doctors we pay for, as often as is reasonable.

clauses.part: Part E — Duties After an Accident or Loss
clauses.text: Allow us to obtain your medical records and other documents about the injuries, and give us a written account of the loss if we ask for one.

clauses.part: Part E — Duties After an Accident or Loss
clauses.text: If the vehicle at fault drove off without being identified, report it to the police within 24 hours.

clauses.part: Part E — Duties After an Accident or Loss
clauses.text: If you sue an uninsured driver, send us a copy of the lawsuit and of any papers you receive in that case.

clauses.part: Part E — Duties After an Accident or Loss
clauses.text: Take reasonable steps to keep the vehicle from further damage; we pay back what you spend doing so.

clauses.part: Part E — Duties After an Accident or Loss
clauses.text: If the vehicle or any of its parts was stolen, report it to the police immediately.

clauses.part: Part E — Duties After an Accident or Loss
clauses.text: Let us see and appraise the vehicle before you repair it or get rid of it.
If an insured goes bankrupt or becomes insolvent, Autos Poblado still owes what this policy covers.
This contract changes only in writing, through an endorsement we issue. If a change you request alters the risk, we adjust the premium from the date of the change.
We give no coverage to anyone who knowingly lied about or hid an important fact about the accident, the loss or the information given to us when buying the policy.
No one may sue us over this policy without first meeting the duties it sets, and the suit must be filed within the deadline set in the Corvane jurisdiction document.
When we pay for harm that someone else caused, we may collect what we paid from that person in place of the insured. The insured helps us do so and does nothing to undermine it.
The policy covers accidents and losses that happen during the policy period shown on the declarations page and within the territory of Corvane.

You may cancel the policy at any time by telling us in writing. We may cancel it only with the advance notice the Corvane jurisdiction document requires, and we refund the premium for the time that had not yet run.
Your rights under this policy do not pass to anyone else without our written consent.
If two or more Autos Poblado policies cover the same accident, the most we pay is the highest limit of any single one of them.
